Retool

Give operators a focused workspace over existing data.

ROfficial product ↗Open in the hierarchy →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Retool can bring databases and APIs into operational applications without rebuilding every interface from the beginning. We can build a workspace where a team sees enquiries, updates records, approves changes, or handles exceptions in one place. Each screen is designed around a real task, with explicit permissions and confirmation steps for actions that alter business data.

Useful outputs

  • Role-specific operational screens
  • Validated forms and action queries
  • Permission model and operator guidance

Where we can apply it

  • Lead desk: new enquiry → operator qualification → CRM ownership update.
  • Inventory approvals: change request → manager review → database update.
  • Automation support: failed execution → exception review → controlled retry.
01

Use case 1

Build a lead assignment console with owner, status, history, and next action.

02

Use case 2

Create inventory or finance approval screens over an existing database.

03

Use case 3

Review failed automations and give an operator a controlled retry action.

Inputs we need

  • Database schema and authorized API access
  • Operator roles and approved actions
  • Current approval and exception process

Delivery sequence

  • Map the task, data sources, and permitted actions for each role.
  • Build connected screens with validation and deliberate write controls.
  • Test user permissions, failure states, and the handover to operators.

Expert review points

  • Verify each role can access only its required records.
  • Approve any destructive action and audit requirements.

We confirm available integrations, plans, permissions, and data mapping before implementing these connection candidates.

  • Supabase
  • PostgreSQL
  • HTTP APIs
  • n8n

Signals we can make visible

  • Task completion time
  • Approval cycle time
  • Exception resolution time

We agree the source, population, period, denominator, and decision behind each measure.
